newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland invites bids for Baltic fleet PZB.
newsitem.headline: Poland invites bids for Baltic fleet PZB.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry is inviting bids for a stake of not less than 10 percent in Polska Zegluga Baltycka SA (PZB), a shipping firm operating in the Baltic region, the ministry said on Friday.
It said in a newspaper advertisement that investors had until September to place bids.

It said that under Polish law employees would receive up to 15 percent of the firm's shares free and five percent would be earmarked for the government progamme to compensate former owners for property confiscated under the communist rule.
At least 10 percent of shares in the company would be used to finance the planned reform of the social security system.
PZB services ferry lines between the Polish coastal cities of Gdansk, Swinoujscie and the Nordic countries.
The company, based in the city of Kolobrzeg, owns five ferries, seven smaller ships, two ferry hubs and a commercial port in Kolobrzeg, with loading capacity of 350,000 tonnes.
PZB serviced 383,800 passengers last year and carried 74,930 cars and 19,956 commercial vehicles.
The company employed 1,800 people in 1995 and had a net profit of two million zlotys. No other financial data of the company were immediately available.
